newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Jan 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Jan 15.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Wednesday's edition of The Wall Street Journal:
- Intel's profit more than doubled in the fourth quarter on the strength of booming international corporate demand.
- Placer Dome offered to acquire Bre-X for stock valued at $4.5 billion.
- KLA Instruments said it agreed to acquire Tencor Instruments in a stock swap valued at $1.3 billion.
- Amtrak's quarterly loss more than doubled.
- The South's tight labor market is extending into higher-paying jobs and is beginning to threaten the region's recent healthy economic growth.
- Retail sales rose 0.6 percent in December.
- Stocks and bonds rose on the tame outlook for inflation.

- Federal credit-union regulator Norman D'Amours was accused by a House Banking Committee member of abusing his authority and engaging in "activities unbecoming of the chairman of a federal regulatory agency."
- The Supreme Court made it easier for workers at some small firms to file suits claiming job bias.
- Enron is expected to announce an alliance to manage the energy needs of 11 California cities that could serve as a model for other public-private partnerships under deregulation.
- The effort by Ameritech effort to become the first Baby Bell to offer long-distance service is in trouble because of errors in its filing with the FCC.
- Philip Morris is preparing to push into the record business, developing some novel tactics to market its Virginia Slims brand to young women.
- Orange County returned to the municipal bond market with an unusual $136 million deal that escaped the notice of many participants for a week.
- Wall Street is talking about yet another turnaround at Equitable Cos, the big insurance company whose shares were flat last year even as the market and shares of other life insurers soared.
